metas.name: Architecture - Ankara
metas.note: Within Ankara you can find many large townhouses, often with triangular roofs and sharp painted and/or mosaic patterns.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Ankara Outskirts
metas.note: Meanwhile the outskirts of Ankara are infamous for their urban sprawl, with strange skyscraper cities in the middle of Central Anatolian nothingness.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Bartin
metas.note: In older parts of Bartın you will find many old all-wooden houses.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Bilecik Mud Bricks
metas.note: In Bilecik and large parts of neighbouring provinces like Bursa, Bolu and Sakarya, you can commonly find the combination of timber-framed houses with mud bricks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Bozcaada
metas.note: Houses on Bozcaada feature many brightly coloured houses with wooden shutters and often wooden second floor façades.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Cow Dung
metas.note: In remote villages in far eastern Turkey you can find cow dung being used as a construction material, mostly for walls. Cow dung ‘bricks’ or ‘slabs’ are often kept in large, very recognisable piles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Diyarbakır
metas.note: The city of Diyarbakır is one of the poorest cities in Turkey and the largest in the southeast, consequently, it has many slums. These differ heavily from those in Adana however, with equally narrow streets but far taller buildings creating lots of dark alleys. The pavement visible in the image is unique to these slums.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Diyarkakir Center
metas.note: The old center of Diyarbakır however is a very strange place. Much of it was destroyed during the Turkish-Kurdish conflict in 2016 and now much is being rebuilt in this unique, oddly clean, modern style, with a lot of dark grey clean-cut bricks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Düzce
metas.note: In Düzce province, you can often find clean timber-framed houses with well-defined edges and colours.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Elmali
metas.note: One noteworthy cluster of wood-framed houses outside the northwest is in the Elmalı valley in Antalya province. Here the frames are notably intricate with many small beams packed together and eight beams meeting at one point - rare in the NW.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Grass Roofs
metas.note: In the inland northeast of Turkey it is very common in villages to find low stone structures with grass roofs - these are mostly storehouses although rarely they constitute actual houses.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Kahramanmaraş
metas.note: Kahramanmaraş was the worst-affected city by the 2023 earthquake. As a result, even though a lot of the coverage was taken two years later, you will still find a lot of rubble, construction sites and empty lots here. (Similar scenes can be seen less frequently in neighbouring provinces)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Kars
metas.note: Older buildings in the city of Kars will usually be made of this unique black tuff.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Kastamonu
metas.note: Kastamonu timber-framed houses often feature a pattern of downward-pointing bricks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Kayseri
metas.note: These larger blocks made of volcanic stone are very common in the architecture of Kayseri.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Kurdish Mountain Villages
metas.note: Villages in more remote and mountainous parts of the Southeast, particularly in provinces like Siirt and Bitlis, have a distinct architecture consisting of flat-topped, tightly-packed stone houses. These are also identifiable from afar as house clusters look like ‘steps’ on the mountainside.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Mugla Chimney
metas.note: The city of Muğla (and to a lesser extent other towns in Muğla province) have these very unique chimneys which have openings on four sides and little flashings on top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Ne Coast
metas.note: Whereas the northwest of Turkey features a lot of traditional architecture with wooden elements, the northeastern coastal hills (roughly from Ordu province eastwards) feature almost entirely concrete buildings even in remote villages, as the extreme humidity of this region makes more traditional materials less viable.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Ottoman
metas.note: Ottoman architecture is characterised by plain-white walls with wooden window frames and shutters, as well as wooden outlines on most (but not all) buildings and an overhanging second floor. It correlates well with the original homeland of the Ottomans in the Northwest (particularly around Bolu). Some historical towns (e.g. Safranbolu, Taraklı) even have predominantly Ottoman architecture.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Prince Islands
metas.note: The Prince Islands off the coast of Istanbul are famous for their predominantly wood panel, all-white, elegant architecture. The islands are also car-free, so the only vehicles you’ll see will be trikes and bikes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Syriac Architecture
metas.note: Tur Abdin is a cultural region in Eastern Mardin centered around Midyat. It is the cultural center of Syriac Orthodox Christianity and many buildings here have a very unique design defined by blocky buildings made of ‘Malta stone’, rich decoration and frequent use of balustrades. There is also a rarer ‘diamond stone’ wall type that is found here. The architectural influences of this area extend beyond it too. Certain features such as the stone type and prominent arches, as well as twin semi-circle windows on façades, extend into villages in southern Batman too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Architecture - Usak Stone
metas.note: Because of the volcanic nature of Uşak, stone houses are more common here than other parts of Western Turkey. These are either white-beige, with a mix of large and small stones, or made of darker brown-grey stone. Quoins are common too. (This looks similar to houses in some regions further east such as Konya, however Uşak is the only region where this type of stone is abundant outside of mountains).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Chevrons - Single Yellow on Black
metas.note: Single type yellow on black chevrons are almost exclusive to Balıkesir province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Chevrons - Yellow Edge
metas.note: Chevrons with yellow edges are found mainly in four provinces; İstanbul, Sakarya, Bursa in the northwest, and Adana in the south. They are rarely found in other provinces(see the map below) NOTE: İstanbul, Bursa and Adana mainly use double type chevrons. When you see single type chevrons with yellow edges and the landscape does not look Mediterranean, you are likely to be in Sakarya.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Cultural - Alawites
metas.note: Alawites are a unique sect within Shiism who are pretty much only found in Hatay (especially southern Hatay). Their mosques look completely different, usually being small, lacking a minaret, and painted all white, often with green highlights.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Cultural - Arabic Signs
metas.note: There is a substantial Arab population living in certain border provinces like Şanlıurfa, Kilis and Mardin, as well as large numbers of refugees in those regions. These are most common in the border towns of Akçakale and Nusaybin, and to a lesser extent in Şanlıurfa and Kilis.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Cultural - Bulgarian Signs
metas.note: In towns near the Bulgarian border you can sometimes find Bulgarian translations on signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Cultural - Kurds
metas.note: Kurds are an Iranic ethnic group that populate much of Southeastern Turkey. In some of the most Kurdish provinces such as Mardin, Şırnak, Hakkâri or Diyarbakır you can occasionally find signage in Kurdish. Kurdish bilingual road signs are particularly common in Diyarbakır and less so in Mardin. The Kurdish language is identified by the presence of circumflex accents (e.g. ê, î) as well as letters that Turkish lacks such as ‘q’, ‘w’ and ‘x’.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Cultural - Russian Signs
metas.note: In Antalya and nearby tourist resorts you will sometimes find Russian signs as the area is very popular with Russian tourists.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Cultural - Shiism
metas.note: Iğdır is the only Shia-majority province of Turkey (not counting Alevis/Alawites). In Shiite areas you will often see black flags with Arabic slogans on them (even without sometimes), as well as pictures of Husseyn.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Akmercan
metas.note: Akmercan is another trans-provincial company that is worth learning for more advanced players. Plaques are either divided into 3 colours, or feature the logo quite prominently.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Aksa
metas.note: Aksa Doğalgaz is found in many different provinces, although together they form three memorable ‘clusters’ for regionguessing. Aksa plaques are generally all yellow with the logo/name either on the top or the bottom corner and the Tel. number 187 on the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.note: Anadolu Yakası (AYEDAŞ)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Edirne Town Entry
metas.note: The province of Edirne has these unique town entry signs with a trapezoid welcome sign followed by the province name (Edirne), followed by the district, followed by the municipality.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Gallipoli Signs
metas.note: The Gallipoli peninsula (the European part of Çanakkale province) is famous for the WWI battles fought between Anzac forces of the British Empire and the Ottoman Empire. You will often find unique yellow-on-brown road signs here indicating tourist sites. There is also ample trekker coverage of the military cemeteries here, so if you get a cemetery trekker, go Gallipoli.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Gazdas
metas.note: Gazdaş has two main divisions - Trakya and Gaziantep. The first operates in the three Thracian provinces of Edirne, Kırklareli and Tekirdağ, whereas the second operates in Gaziantep and Kilis. Its plaques are yellow, red and white, similar to some Akmercan plaques.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Gaziantep
metas.note: Gaziantep ‘cute trams’
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - İl Özel İdaresi
metas.note: İl Özel İdaresi (İÖİ) - Bollards in these provinces often carry the insignia ‘İl Özel İdaresi’ meaning “special province district”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Istanbul
metas.note: Istanbul trams will always have the ‘Metro Istanbul’ symbol on either end (also found at metro stations).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.note: İzmir
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Karabük
metas.note: Karabük
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Kargaz
metas.note: Kargaz operates in 3 provinces: Karabük, Kastamonu and Çankırı. Its plaques are relatively simple and have the logo in the bottom right.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Kirgaz
metas.note: Kırgaz operates in both ‘Kır’ provinces (Kırşehir and Kırıkkale) and has these unique white plaques.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Kocaeli
metas.note: Kocaeli
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oil Fields
metas.note: Oil fields are a good meta for Batman province, particularly just south of Batman city. They exist in other provinces too, but are far more common here than anywhere else. You will also rarely see oil fields in eastern Adıyaman.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Osmangazi
metas.note: Osmangazi
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Rumble Stripes Eastern
metas.note: The only places where you will find rumble strips on the classic 4-lane no-divider eastern roads is the highways just outside of Van and Yüksekova.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.note: Samsun

metas.note: Trakya - Numbers can be red or black
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Wind Farms
metas.note: Wind turbines are mostly found in the far west of the country, particularly the northwest. Particularly strong hotspots include Balıkesir province, western Istanbul and the Karabunar peninsula and Yenişakran areas in İzmir province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yeşilırmak
metas.note: Yeşilırmak
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Adana Plain
metas.note: The Adana plain is one of the largest expanse of flat land in Turkey with a subtropical landscape.The southwest is deadflat with very mixed agriculture consisting of different fruit and vegetable fields as well as cotton and corn, with subtropical plants such as eucalyptus, palms and reeds being common in between. Mountains will normally be visible to the northwest.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Afyonkarahisar
metas.note: The city of Afyonkarahisar has numerous small but steep-sided hills in the middle of town that can appear very close even on very urban rounds.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Aladaglari
metas.note: In Aladağları Milli Park (National Park) you will find a huge steep wall of mountains to your east which is highly recognisable, even from some distance.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Amasya
metas.note: The city of Amasya is tightly bound within a valley surrounded by rocky hills. The city centre is overlooked by a hill with a castle on top and imposing Pontic tombs carved within it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Antalya
metas.note: Much of Antalya province is very recognisable for its forests composed entirely of Turkish pines combined with a rocky karst landscape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Ararat
metas.note: Mount Ararat is the tallest peak in Turkey and the tallest in the Middle East outside Iran. It is particularly recognisable as it also has a prominent secondary peak called Masis. It is situated near the Armenian border on the border between Ağrı (its Turkish name) province and Iğdır province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Balik Gölü
metas.note: Balık Gölü is one of two lakes in far eastern Turkey (beside Lake Van) situated within a pristine, green steppe-like environment. The other is Çıldır Gölü, the main distinction being that Balık Gölü is smaller and surrounded by mountains.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Bitlis
metas.note: Bitlis is one of the smallest provincial capitals. It is a very green city surrounded by dry mountains. The city itself is also very historical, with a huge castle in the middle and lots of old stone mosques.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Burdur Gölü
metas.note: Burdur is a saline lake in the west of Turkey, and therefore contained within a valley surrounded by mountains (unlike the salt lakes of Central Anatolia). The only other such lake is Acı Gölü just north of it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Cappadocia
metas.note: Cappadocia is a very unique and famous area in Central Turkey just east of Nevşehir which is highly distinct for its ‘fairy chimneys’. In the absence of these you can still identify the region through it’s exposed hillsides made of pink and white rock and general ‘Utah-like’ landscape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Central Volcanic Hills
metas.note: Stretching from Southern Nevşehir to Karapınar in Konya province are a range of long-extinct volcanoes. In the flatter parts between these volcanoes, where you will find more coverage, you will find numerous isolated, smooth-sloped volcanic hills which are largely unique to this area. (You can find somewhat similar hills in Northern Konya).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Cildir Gölü
metas.note: Çıldır Gölü is the other far-eastern steppe lake, situated much further north near the Georgian border. It is larger, greener, and surrounded by gentler slopes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Hatay Northern Half
metas.note: Meanwhile, the northern half going into Gaziantep forms a more narrow valley with mountains clearly visible on either side. Here you will also find rock walls made of large orange boulders, as well as a more rocky landscape more generally.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Hatay South
metas.note: Eastern Hatay has a superflat landscape, however unlike the Central Plateau, the soil here is quite red and you will always be able to see mountains to your east & west. It can be divided in two parts - the southern half is wider and more featureless, with mountains often quite distant.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Mardin
metas.note: Eastern Mardin has a very distinct landscape of low, craggy hills covered in stone walls and scattered vegetation.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Taurus
metas.note: The Eastern Taurus are the high mountains that form a chain roughly from Bingöl to south of Lake Van. Like Tunceli, they also form islands of forests in the Southeast, although the soil is less red and the whole region is visibly drier. The valleys will also be full of black poplars
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Erciyes
metas.note: Mount Erciyes is the second tallest volcano in Turkey after Mount Ararat. It is located south of the city of Kayseri where it can be seen for some distance, and is particularly identifiable for the numerous volcanic ridges and sub-peaks surrounding the main peak (which is usually not visible).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Erzincan Plain
metas.note: Erzincan is situated in a relatively narrow plain with particularly high mountains on both sides, with high peaks to the northeast and southeast. The valley also has a moderate amount of tree cover with black poplars and willows being common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Hasandag
metas.note: Another important volcano is Hasandağ southeast of the city of Aksaray. Unlike Erciyes it is a more clear cone volcano and due to the dryness of Aksaray province its peak is more likely to be visible.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Igdir
metas.note: Most of Iğdır province is covered by the Arax plain, shared with Armenia. Here you’ll find a flat landscape covered in grassy fields and loads of black poplars. The best indication that you are here is Mount Ararat to the south, but it can sometimes be hard to see. Besides the landscape, villages in Iğdır usually consist of houses made of large, plain grey bricks and sheet metal roofs, and you’ll also find a lot of tall haystacks here.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Karaburun Ppeninsula
metas.note: The Karaburun Peninsula is one of the most mountainous parts of the west coast, and has a unique landscape of either low spongy bushes or olive plantations, often with wind farms visible in the background. The southern part of the peninsula is less mountainous but has a lot of small rocks all over the ground.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Karacadag
metas.note: Karacadağ is a wide, gently-rising volcanic hill with a unique barren, red soil and bushy landscape. The hill itself can be recognised from afar as a gently rising hill with a black stone peak. The area around it is also covered in volcanic rocks. Fun fact, it is on the slopes of this hill that the first evidence of wheat domestication was discovered.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Kastamonu
metas.note: Kastamonu is essentially a small plateau within the northern mountains, which is drier and more piney than anywhere else in the north, with a landscape of agricultural, gently-rolling hills, often with slightly taller greener hills visible in the distance. The northern half of this plateau around Devrekani is particular distinct for its mixture of bare with lots of exposed rocks and dry all-pine forests.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Kilis Hills
metas.note: The only similar area to Eastern Mardin (see above) is the hills of Kilis and Gaziantep. The key difference is that these hills are volcanic, meaning the stones and soil are darker, and you will also find more agriculture and fewer scattered bushes in the shallow valleys.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Konya
metas.note: The Konya plain is the flattest part of Turkey and also very green and agricultural in relation to other parts of the Anatolian plateau. Note that the plain stretches east from Konya to the city Karapınar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Köse Dagi
metas.note: Köse Dağı is the highest peak of the Aras range, located to the northwest of the Ağrı valley. Being far more prominent than the surrounding peaks, and having a relatively smooth shape, it is a good way to identify the valley.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Küre Daglari
metas.note: Within the northern forested mountains of Turkey there is one area that is topographically very different from the rest, situated in Bartın province very near the coast covered by the Küre Mountains National Park. What’s unique about these mountains is that they form a plateau with steep cliffs on most sides which are visible from numerous angles, very different from the interlocking peaks in the rest of the north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Malatya
metas.note: North of the city of Malatya is a relatively large flat agricultural area which can look very uncharacteristic for the east. Most of Turkey’s apricots are grown here, so recognising apricot trees can help, otherwise you may be able to see dry mountains from the area, which should indicate you are in Malatya rather than other fruit-producing regions.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Medetsiz Tepe
metas.note: Medetsiz Tepe is one of the highest massifs in the Taurus Mountains forming a fairly long, roughly east-west ridge, which is visible from a stretch of the D750 and some remote villages and mountain roads as a wall of snow-capped mountains to the south.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Menderes Massif
metas.note: The Menderes Massif is a unique geological area covering much of Aydın province. Here you’ll find a lot of grey boulders and exposed rock, leading to the construction of lots of stone walls. Stone pines are also exceedingly common in this region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Mut Landscape
metas.note: Around the town of Mut in western Mersin province, you will find a unique karst landscape of white soil with a mix of conical and table mountains and generally crazy topography, all surrounded by fruit tree plantations.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Nur Mountains 1
metas.note: The Nur Mountains is the range that runs the length of Hatay Province. They are identifiable in various ways - certain types of infrastructure in a green mountainous setting are especially common in Hatay, metal mesh poles and ‘southeast houses’ with flat roofs. Another distinct feature of these mountains is how ‘high up’ many rounds seem. While the Hatay mountains are far from the highest, they rise extremely precipitously, giving the illusion of being incredibly tall when looking down at the coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Red Soil
metas.note: North of Gaziantep, leaking a bit into Şanlıurfa province, you can find extreme dark red soils, mostly covered in pistachio or olive plantations.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Salt Pans
metas.note: In the middle of the Anatolian plateau you can find a number of salt pans, the largest being Tuz Gölü (lit. ‘salt lake’) at the tripoint of Konya, Aksaray and Ankara provinces. Around these lakes you will find a deadflat, pale landscape with very minimal vegetation consisting mostly of thistles. Sometimes the salt lakes themselves will be visible.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Strandzha
metas.note: Strandzha is a hill range on the Bulgarian border in the northern part of European Turkey. It consists of low but very green hills, however it can be extremely difficult to tell apart from other parts of North Turkey. Besides a general ‘European forest vibe’, other clues for Strandzha are small, empty grassy clearings by the roadside, young cottonwood plantations, and yellow bollards which, whilst not exclusive to Kırklareli, are common here while very rare in the rest of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Süphan Dagi
metas.note: Süphan Dağı is an isolated, snow-capped volcano on the northern shore of Lake Van, which makes it an excellent reference point for pinpointing your position on the lake, but also for the remote dirt roads to the north of the mountain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Tunceli
metas.note: Tunceli is unusually green for an eastern province. It is distinguishable from other forested parts of the country as its forests consist exclusively of oak trees, with slightly reddish soil and exposed dark grey mountain sides further confirming the province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Uludag
metas.note: Uludağ is the highest mountain in the northwest of Turkey. It is useful for identifying Bursa and the plain around it, as the mountain creates a huge, cloud-shrouded wall to the south.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Usak
metas.note: Uşak sits on an ancient volcanic basin (technically a northern extension of the Menderes Massif) meaning you will see a lot of scattered rocks on the ground, although these are much lighter coloured than in the Menderes Massif. (This is quite subtle but still useful in flatter, more agricultural areas).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - White Bluffs
metas.note:
There is a large area between the cities of Ankara and Eskişehir that is full of these low hills with exposed white hillsides, with a generally green, agricultural, but mostly treeless landscape beside it.

A smaller cluster of these exposed hillsides can be found in Çankırı province, where they are more pronounced and have marked striations.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - D400
metas.note: The part of the D400 that runs along the Iraqi border is very recognisable. It runs through a narrow and very dry canyon with lots of poplars and a small stream (the border itself) at the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - D885
metas.note: The D885 between Tunceli and Pülümür is quite recognisable. It goes through a typical Tunceli landscape (see above) however it consistently follows a stream with the road following the bottom of a valley. Furthermore, at many points along the road you’ll find these mini tunnels, and there is frequent graffiti/political posters for Kurdish militant groups (PKK/HPG) and the left-wing HDP party (vastly more popular in Kurdish regions than other parts of the country - posters are always purple).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - D915
metas.note: The D915, or ‘Turkey’s death road’ (not an official title, you heard it here first) is extremely recognisable. It crosses over the mountains between Bayburt and Of - the highest part consists only of a thin gravel road with a steep drop on one side.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - E99
metas.note: The E99 leading into Azerbaijan is very identifiable. It is a very straight NW-SE road leading through a wetlands environment with dry mountains on either side. Mount Ararat is faintly visible to the northwest.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - O-52
metas.note: Along the following stretches of the O-52 you will find a lane of fresh dark asphalt in the outer lane on both sides of the motorway.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - Samandağ-kale
metas.note: The coastal road around Musa Dağ (Hatay) is identifiable by the segregated cycle path that follows the length of the road between Kale and Samandağ.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Alder
metas.note: Alder (Alnus glutinosa) can be recognized by its round leaves and pronounced leaf veins. It is very concentrated in the northeast of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Almonds
metas.note: Almonds are a decent meta for Adıyaman province when found in isolated plantations. Another noteworthy hotspot in the southwest however is the Datça peninsula. where they grow abundantly.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Apples
metas.note: The valleys around Eğirdir Gölü in Isparta account for most of Turkey’s apple production.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Black Pine
metas.note: European black pine (Pinus nigra) is widely found in the northern and southwestern mountains, but it is very rare in the center of Anatolian plateau and eastern part of the country. This species features a lot of clusters of needles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cabbage
metas.note: Samsun province produces the vast majority of Turkey’s cabbages, and most of those are produced in the flat Bafra district that sticks out from the coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Caucasian Spruce
metas.note: Caucasian spruce (Picea orientalis) is the only spruce species found in Turkey, and it is most common in the far northeastern part of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cedar
metas.note: Lebanon cedar (Cedrus libani), which can be recognized by their big cones and fairly horizontal branches and leaves, is found in high mountains along the Mediterranean coast. NOTE: This species is often found planted in central-western plateau, in much shorter height. When the terrain is not mountainous, you should better ignore these trees.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cherries
metas.note: Cherries are mainly produced in three distinct areas - the Kemalpaşa valley just east of İzmir, the Sultandağı valley stretching south to Akşehir and the Bursa Valley just northeast of Bursa city, where it grows alongside many other fruit. Cherries can be recognised in spring by pink cherryblossoms and in summer by their short trunks and tall branches with long droopy leaves. And in summer by their short trunks and tall branches with long droopy leaves.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Citrus
metas.note: Citrus plantations are found on much of the Mediterranean coast from Aydın all the way to Hatay, being most common in the Adana plain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cypress
metas.note: Mediterranean cypress (Cupressus sempervirens) is a conifer tree that features a very sharp crown resembling a spear and is mainly found along the south coast and the southern west coast, but also less commonly in the northwest of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Eucalyptus
metas.note: Eucalyptus is restricted to the southern and western coastal parts of the country, with particular concentrations in certain areas such as Muğla. In an agricultural setting between fields, it is essentially unique to the Adana plain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Fan Palm
metas.note: Fan palms (Washingtonia robusta) are, as the name suggests, palms featuring fan-shaped leaves and are a good clue that you are somewhere along the south coast, especially around the cities of Antalya and Adana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Ferns
metas.note: Ferns in Turkey are mainly found along the north coast and less commonly in other coastal areas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Figs
metas.note: Aydın province produces 70% of Turkey’s figs, with most of the rest produced just across the border in İzmir.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Firs
metas.note: Firs (Abies spp.) are difficult to tell apart from other conifers, but the biggest clue lies in their branching structure, each branch coming off the trunk shaped like a flat fan. When viewed from the right angle you can often see the layers of flat branches stacked on top of one another. This contrasts with the branching structure of spruces, where secondary branches usually droop down from the primary branch. It is most common in the central northern mountains.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Grapes
metas.note: Besides the dense vineyards of the Alaşehir valley, there are a few other grape producing regions of Turkey. Just east of this valley, north of Denizli, is a unique red soil landscape with low, sporadic vineyards. There are also vineyards in the valley near the Gaziantep-Hatay border, particularly just south of İslahiye, as well as small isolated vineyards spread around Thrace and Cappadoccia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Greenhouses
metas.note: Along the southern coast of Turkey you will find numerous dense clusters of plastic and glass greenhouses. The westernmost of these clusters is around Kınık on the Muğla-Antalya border and the easternmost lies just east of Mersin. Note that individual greenhouses can be found all over the country, it is best to use this meta if you find greenhouses on multiple sides.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Hazelnuts
metas.note: Hazelnuts absolutely dominate the landscape of much of the forested northern parts of the country. It is cultivated throughout the coastal hills from Kocaeli province all the way to Artvin, however it is especially dominant in Ordu, Giresun and Sakarya (usually in the latter province they are found in a flatter landscape). Hazelnut trees can be identified by their multiple thin stems emanating from a single point and round leaves. Hazelnut-covered mountains are even distinct from afar as they have a seemingly fuzzy texture with a sort of green-purple colour.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Hungarian Oak
metas.note: Hungarian oak (Quercus frainetto) is one of several oak species found in Turkey and can be recognized by the shape of its leaves. It has typical oak leaves, but they are larger and more deeply lobed than on other oak species.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Inland Greenhouses
metas.note: Greenhouses in a drier, more inland landscape, often without roofs, are common in the Elmalı valley and neighbouring inland regions of Western Antalya province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Mastic
metas.note: Mastic is a common Mediterranean shrub that can be used to identify the southwest coast, although it does exist less commonly up to halfway down the southern coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Opium
metas.note: White opium poppies, yes you heard that right, are cultivated licitly in the valley around Afyonkarahisar, and they are very recognisable. A good mnemonic for this is that the name ‘Afyon-kara-hisar’ literally translates as ‘opium-black-fortress’.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pears
metas.note: Pears are mostly produced in the aforementioned Bursa valley.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pickly Pear
metas.note: Prickly pear (Opuntia ficus-indica) is a type of cactus that consists of flat round pads and is found along the south coast and southern west coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pistachios
metas.note: Pistachios are mainly grown around Gaziantep.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Poplar Plantations
metas.note: Also known as ‘Düzce trees’ - while poplar plantations can be found here and there in most temperate parts of Turkey, large orderly plantations are particularly common in the Düzce and Sakarya valleys.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Rice
metas.note: Rice is most common along the Greek border, and in northern Balıkesir, however it can be found in a few other distinct hotspots in the flat ‘deltas’ of Samsun province, numerous river valleys in Çorum, Sinop and Çankırı, and eastern Hatay.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Scots Pine
metas.note: Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris) is recognized most easily by its red bark, but beware that the bottom section of the trunk is generally darker and not red. You can find it in inland regions along the north coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Stone Pine
metas.note: Stone pine (Pinus pinea) can be recognized by its rounded crown, where all the branches and needles are concentrated towards the top of the tree. It is found predominantly along the west coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Turkish Pine
metas.note: Turkish pine (Pinus brutia) is perhaps the most difficult pine species to identify in Turkey. It tends to have a less dense crown and brighter needles than other pines, the bark can be brown and can sometimes have a red tinge, but there is no stark contrast between the bottom and top sections of the trunk as there is with Scots pine. It is mainly found along the south and west coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Vegetation - Van Mullein
metas.note: In northern Van there are numerous remote/dirt roads with ‘yellow flower spam’. Known as mullein (Verbascum sp.), it is very distinct for its tall stem with yellow flowers all along it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.
